newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end soft despite interest rate drop.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end soft despite interest rate drop.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed off in moderate trade, failing to take heart from falling interest rates and strong gains in national telephone company CANTV, traders said.
Benchmark six-month interest rates fell 165 basis points to 15.20 percent on high local liquidity at the Central Bank's regular TEM auction.

Falling interest rates boost prospects for higher company earnings. But the market's leading 19-share index slipped 1.29 percent to close at 6,324.66 points as 48 million stocks traded worth 4.3 billion bolivars ($9.2 million).
"The day got off to a slow start, but roused itself a bit with the fall in TEM rates and the rise in CANTV," said Banesco broker Simon Brad.

CANTV shares soared 132 bolivars in early trade to close at 2,000 as the stock caught up with Monday and Tuesday gains in its American Depository Receipts on the New York Stock Exchange. The Caracas bolsa was closed for Carnival for the first two days of the week.
"CANTV is looking strong," Multinvest broker Jose Gregorio Tineo, who saw further gains ahead.
Among the day's traded issues, 21 fell, 10 rose and five closed flat.
Volume was boosted by a cross trade of 39 million B shares in real estate fund Fondo de Valores Inmobilarios, majority-owned by New York-based financial guru George Soros.
The stock closed off 0.25 bolivars at 37.00.
